text_blocks.snippet: Esophagitis, or inflammation of the esophagus, can be caused by a variety of factors. The most common cause is gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), where stomach acid flows back into the esophagus. Other causes include certain medications, infections, and allergic reactions, particularly eosinophilic esophagitis.
snippet_highlighted_words: gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), where stomach acid flows back into the esophagus.
Other causes include certain medications, infections, and allergic reactions, particularly eosinophilic esophagitis

list.snippet: Stomach acid, bile, and other digestive fluids can irritate and damage the esophageal lining when they flow backward into the esophagus.
This is the most frequent cause of esophagitis.
Certain medications, particularly when taken without enough water or while lying down, can irritate the esophagus.
Examples include NSAIDs (like aspirin and ibuprofen), certain antibiotics (like doxycycline), and osteoporosis medications (like alendronate).
Infections, often in individuals with weakened immune systems, can cause inflammation.
Common culprits include fungal infections like Candida, viral infections like herpes simplex and cytomegalovirus.
This is an allergic condition where a type of white blood cell (eosinophil) accumulates in the esophagus, leading to inflammation.
It's often triggered by food allergies or environmental allergens.
Vomiting: Frequent or severe vomiting can cause chemical burns in the esophagus.
Radiation Therapy: Radiation treatment for cancers in the chest or neck can damage the esophageal lining.
Allergies: Food allergies can trigger inflammation, especially in eosinophilic esophagitis.
Smoking: Tobacco smoke can irritate the esophagus and contribute to inflammation.
Alcohol: Excessive alcohol consumption can also irritate the esophagus.
Hiatal Hernia: This condition, where part of the stomach protrudes through the diaphragm, can contribute to GERD and esophagitis.
